queries: WITH qualified AS (SELECT ID FROM Laboratory GROUP BY ID HAVING SUM(CASE WHEN `U-PRO` = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0 AND SUM(CASE WHEN RA = '-' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) > 0), per_patient AS (SELECT l.ID, AVG(l.PT) AS avg_pt, AVG(l.TAT - l.TAT2) AS avg_diff FROM Laboratory l JOIN qualified q ON q.ID = l.ID GROUP BY l.ID) SELECT AVG(avg_pt) AS avg_of_avg_pt, AVG(avg_diff) AS avg_of_avg_tat_diff FROM per_patient

assumptions.assumption: The per-patient average of TAT minus TAT2 is computed only over records where both TAT and TAT2 are non-null (the difference is NULL otherwise and is ignored). Patients with no non-null values for a metric are skipped in that metric's overall average.

assumptions.assumption: TAT - TAT2 is computed per row, so rows where either TAT or TAT2 is NULL are ignored for that average. Each patient's average is over the remaining rows.
Patients whose per-patient average is NULL (all PT values missing, or no row with both TAT and TAT2) are ignored in the final average, because AVG skips NULLs.

alternatives.interpretation: Compute the TAT and TAT2 averages separately, each ignoring its own missing values, and then subtract: AVG(TAT) - AVG(TAT2) per patient. This uses rows where only one of the two is present.
